title: Weights in grams and kilograms for babies and children
blurb: Convert baby and child weights between grams and kilograms, round to two decimal places correctly and use the weight in kg for doses and feeds.
question: A baby is born weighing 3285 g. A medicine is prescribed per kilogram. What is the baby's weight in kilograms, and why does it matter which unit you use?

teach.h: Grams on the scales, kilograms in the formula
teach.body: 1 kg = 1000 g. Birth weights and neonatal weights are usually recorded in grams (3450 g), but doses and feeds are prescribed per kilogram (mg/kg, mL/kg/day). Plain English: before any per-kg calculation, turn the grams into kilograms by dividing by 1000. 3450 g becomes 3.45 kg.
teach.cite: SI definitions; Pearson midwifery practice paper (g to kg item)

head: Grams
Kilograms
teach.caption: Below 1000 g the kg value starts with 0. Children are usually weighed in kg; convert to g by x 1000.

teach.body: If the question asks for two decimal places, look at the third decimal digit. 5 or more: round the second digit up. Under 5: leave it. 2965 g = 2.965 kg, which rounds to 2.97 kg; 4062 g = 4.062 kg, which rounds to 4.06 kg. Round only the final answer, never a weight you are about to use in a dose.

items: Midwife Grace Adeyemi weighs baby Noah on day 3: 3180 g. His birth weight was 3.4 kg.
Put both in the same unit: 3.4 kg = 3400 g.
Sense check: a couple of hundred grams lost from about three and a half kilograms is a small fraction of the birth weight, so the answer is in the right range.

teach.text: A 3450 g baby is 3.45 kg, not 34.5 kg: a newborn weighing 34.5 kg is impossible, so a quick sense check catches a slipped point. Using grams in a per-kg formula makes the dose 1000 times too large.

items.label: extremely low birth weight baby: starts 0.
error if g is used as kg

items: 1 kg = 1000 g: g to kg ÷ 1000, kg to g x 1000.
Convert the weight to kg before any per-kg dose or feed.
Compare weights only once both are in the same unit.
Two decimal places: check the third digit; 5 or more rounds up.
Sense-check: a newborn weighs a few kilograms.

summary: You can now convert baby and child weights between grams and kilograms, compare weights recorded in different units, round a weight to two decimal places, and use the weight in kilograms for per-kg doses and feeds.

A.q: A baby on a postnatal ward weighs 3720 g. What is the weight in kilograms? Write your answer to two decimal places.

whyNot.0: Divided by 100; g to kg is ÷ 1000.
whyNot.1: Divided by 10000; g to kg is ÷ 1000.
whyNot.2: Divided by 10; g to kg is ÷ 1000.

A.q: A child on a children's ward weighs 14.5 kg. What is the weight in grams?

whyNot.0: Multiplied by 100; kg to g is x 1000.
whyNot.1: Multiplied by 10000; kg to g is x 1000.
whyNot.2: Divided by 1000; going to a smaller unit you multiply.

A.q: A preterm baby on a neonatal unit weighs 0.98 kg. What is the weight in grams?

whyNot.0: Multiplied by 100; kg to g is x 1000.
whyNot.2: Multiplied by 10000; kg to g is x 1000.
whyNot.3: Divided by 1000; going to a smaller unit you multiply.

B.q: A baby's birth weight was 3.4 kg. On day 3 the baby weighs 3150 g. How many grams has the baby lost?

whyNot.0: Subtracted 3.4 from 3150 without converting the units.

B.q: A baby on a children's ward weighs 6350 g and is prescribed a medicine at 15 mg/kg. What dose in milligrams is needed? Write your answer to two decimal places.

whyNot.1: Used the weight in grams; convert to kg first.
whyNot.2: Converted 6350 g to 63.5 kg; g to kg is ÷ 1000.
whyNot.3: Converted 6350 g to 0.635 kg; g to kg is ÷ 1000.

B.q: A baby is born weighing 2965 g. What is the birth weight in kilograms? Write your answer to two decimal places.
B.why: 2965 ÷ 1000 = 2.965 kg. The third decimal is 5, so round up: 2.97 kg.

whyNot.0: Truncated: the third digit is 5, so round up.
whyNot.1: Divided by 100; g to kg is ÷ 1000.
whyNot.3: Not rounded to two decimal places as instructed.

C.q: A baby weighing 2850 g is prescribed feeds of 150 mL/kg/day, given 3-hourly (8 feeds in 24 hours). How many millilitres should each feed be? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.

whyNot.0: This is the daily total; divide by the 8 feeds.
whyNot.1: Divided by 6 feeds; 3-hourly is 8 feeds a day.
whyNot.3: Used the weight in grams; convert to kg first.

C.q: An infant weighed 4.6 kg at 6 weeks and 5120 g at 10 weeks. What was the average weight gain per week in grams?

whyNot.1: This is the total gain over 4 weeks, not per week.
whyNot.2: Subtracted 4.6 from 5120 without converting, then divided by 4.

C.q: A baby's birth weight is 3600 g. By day 3 the baby has lost 10% of the birth weight. What is the day 3 weight in kilograms? Write your answer to two decimal places.

whyNot.0: Added 10% instead of taking it away.
whyNot.2: Converted 3240 g by ÷ 100; g to kg is ÷ 1000.

reteach.title: Kilos on the left, grams on the right
reteach.question: Where does the decimal point go in 3285 g when you write it in kilograms?

blocks.body: Grams to kilograms is ÷ 1000, so count three digits in from the right and place the point there: 3285 g becomes 3.285 kg. The digit before the point is whole kilograms; the three after are the grams.

blocks.text: If a newborn's weight in kg is more than about 6, the point is in the wrong place.

explain.body: Divide by 1000, then apply the rounding instruction to the final figure only.

test.q: Convert 4075 g to kilograms. Write your answer to two decimal places.
test.why: 4075 ÷ 1000 = 4.075; the third decimal is 5, so 4.08 kg.

whyNot.0: Truncated: the third digit is 5, so round up.
whyNot.2: Divided by 100; g to kg is ÷ 1000.
whyNot.3: Divided by 10000; g to kg is ÷ 1000.

explain.body: Multiply by 1000: point three places right, filling with zeros.

test.q: A baby weighs 1.6 kg. What is the weight in grams?

whyNot.1: Multiplied by 100; kg to g is x 1000.
whyNot.2: Multiplied by 10000; kg to g is x 1000.
whyNot.3: Read 1.6 kg as 1 kg and 6 g; 0.6 kg is 600 g.

explain.body: To find a gain or loss, convert both weights to the same unit first.

test.q: A baby weighed 3.25 kg at birth and 3080 g today. How many grams has the baby lost?

explain.text: Per-kg doses need the weight in kg. Grams in the formula give a dose 1000 times too big.

test.q: A baby weighs 3500 g and is prescribed a medicine at 4 mg/kg. What dose in milligrams is needed?

whyNot.0: Used the weight in grams; convert to kg first.
whyNot.2: Converted 3500 g to 0.35 kg; g to kg is ÷ 1000.
whyNot.3: Converted 3500 g to 35 kg; g to kg is ÷ 1000.
